Title: Step-by-Step Synthesis of Tris(2,2′-bipyridine)ruthenium(II) Chloride ([Ru(bpy)₃]Cl₂)

1. Overview  
   • Target compound: tris(2,2′-bipyridine)ruthenium(II) chloride, [Ru(bpy)₃]Cl₂  
   • Yield target: ~60–70% based on RuCl₃·3H₂O  

2. Reagents and Solvents  
   • Ruthenium(III) chloride hydrate (RuCl₃·3H₂O), ≥99% purity, 1.00 g (3.8 mmol)  
   • 2,2′-Bipyridine (bpy), ≥98% purity, 2.25 g (14.4 mmol, 3.8 equiv)  
   • Ethylene glycol (solvent for reflux) or a 1:1 ethanol/water mixture as alternative  
   • Potassium hexafluorophosphate (KPF₆), 1.50 g (8.1 mmol) for metathesis (optional counter-ion exchange)  
   • Deionized water, 200 mL  
   • Ethanol (absolute), 100 mL  

3. Equipment  
   • 250 mL round-bottom flask with three-neck adapter  
   • Reflux condenser  
   • Magnetic stir bar and stir plate  
   • Heating mantle or oil bath  
   • Dropping funnel (optional)  
   • Vacuum filtration apparatus (Büchner funnel, filter paper)  
   • Centrifuge tubes (50 mL) or vacuum centrifuge  
   • Vacuum desiccator or oven  

4. Synthetic Procedure  

Step 1 Complexation (Reflux)  
a. Place 1.00 g RuCl₃·3H₂O and 2.25 g 2,2′-bipyridine into the 250 mL flask.  
b. Add 100 mL ethylene glycol to the flask. Insert the reflux condenser, and begin stirring.  
c. Heat to reflux (≈190 °C) under stirring for 4 hours. The solution will darken (deep red).  

Step 2 Cooling and Precipitation  
a. After 4 h, turn off heat and allow the mixture to cool to ≈50 °C while stirring.  
b. Slowly pour the hot reaction mixture into 200 mL deionized water under stirring. A red precipitate of [Ru(bpy)₃]Cl₂ will form.  

Step 3 Isolation of Crude Complex  
a. Collect the precipitate by vacuum filtration (Büchner funnel).  
b. Wash the solid with cold deionized water (2 × 20 mL) to remove excess salts.  
c. Transfer the wet cake into centrifuge tubes, add 20 mL ethanol, centrifuge and decant. Repeat once.  

Step 4 Counter-Ion Exchange (Optional)  
To obtain [Ru(bpy)₃](PF₆)₂:  
a. Dissolve the crude [Ru(bpy)₃]Cl₂ in 30 mL water.  
b. Add 1.50 g KPF₆ portionwise under stirring. A yellow-orange solid of [Ru(bpy)₃](PF₆)₂ will precipitate.  
c. Filter, wash with water (2 × 10 mL), then ethanol (1 × 10 mL).  

Step 5 Drying  
a. Transfer the filtered solid to a vacuum desiccator or oven at 40 °C.  
b. Dry until constant weight (typically 6–8 h).  

5. Characterization (Key Data)  
• UV-Vis (aqueous): λmax ≈ 452 nm (ε ≈ 14,600 M⁻¹cm⁻¹)  
• 1H NMR (D₂O): signals in 7.2–9.3 ppm region (bipyridine aromatic)  
• Elemental analysis (for [PF₆]⁻ salt): RuC₃₀H₂₀F₁₂N₆P₂Cl₂ fits expected values  

6. Expected Yield and Appearance  
• Yield: 0.9–1.1 g of [Ru(bpy)₃]Cl₂ (~60–70%) or 1.2–1.4 g of [Ru(bpy)₃](PF₆)₂  
• Appearance: deep red crystalline powder (Cl⁻ salt) or yellow-orange microcrystals (PF₆⁻ salt)  

This completes the synthesis of tris(2,2′-bipyridine)ruthenium(II) chloride for advanced photochemical and electrochemical studies.
